title: State judge orders Kalshi to stop offering sports bets and other wagers
gist: A Washington state judge granted a preliminary injunction ordering Kalshi to geofence out sports, election, politics, entertainment, culture, tech/science and 'mentions' wagers by September 2 or face up to $120,000 per day in penalties, ruling that the Commodity Exchange Act contains no express preemption of state gambling law. The CFTC under Chairman Michael Selig is simultaneously fighting on Kalshi's side, having declared a 'market emergency' in New York.

themes.theme: The Washington injunction and its operational bite

insights.claim: King County Superior Court Judge John McHale issued a preliminary injunction requiring prediction market Kalshi to stop offering, accepting or facilitating wagers on sports, elections, politics, entertainment, culture, tech and science, or 'mentions' in Washington state.
insights.speaker: Jon Brodkin
insights.so_what: The first broad state-court shutdown of a prediction market's core contract categories sets a template other AGs can copy.
insights.quote: The order requires Kalshi to stop offering, accepting, or facilitating wagers on sports, elections, politics, entertainment, culture, tech and science, or mentions in Washington
insights.locator: A state court in Washington this week ordered Kalshi

insights.claim: Kalshi must implement an IP address and residency-based geofence by August 19, 2026 and a multi-source geofencing solution by September 2, 2026, with penalties of up to $120,000 per day for failing to complete the ordered geofencing.
insights.speaker: Jon Brodkin
insights.so_what: Compliance is now a hard-dated engineering deliverable with a quantified daily burn rate — a modelable cost line for the company.
insights.quote: Kalshi could face penalties of up to $120,000 per day if it fails to complete the implementation of the ordered geofencing by September 2.
insights.locator: Under the court order, Kalshi could face penalties

insights.claim: Washington Attorney General Nick Brown states the enjoined categories, while not covering all Kalshi wagers, represent a substantial part of a business that in recent years has been increasingly driven by sports wagers.
insights.speaker: Jon Brodkin
insights.so_what: Kalshi's revenue mix has drifted toward sports — the exact category most exposed to state gambling enforcement.
insights.quote: This does not include all the wagers offered on Kalshi, but it includes a substantial part of their business, which in recent years has been increasingly driven by sports wagers.
insights.locator: said a press release yesterday from Washington Attorney General Nick Brown

insights.claim: The court order lets Kalshi users exit positions they already hold, while Washington explicitly reserves the right to seek recovery for fees and losses incurred by Washington consumers on or after September 2, 2026.
insights.speaker: Jon Brodkin
insights.so_what: Contingent clawback liability on post-September-2 Washington volume is an unquantified tail risk sitting behind the injunction.
insights.quote: The State reserves, and does not waive, the right to seek recovery for fees and losses incurred by Washington consumers on or after September 2, 2026
insights.locator: Kalshi will not prohibit users from exiting positions

themes.theme: The preemption question is being resolved against Kalshi

insights.claim: Judge McHale concluded that the US Commodity Exchange Act does not preempt Washington state gambling law, because the statute gives the CFTC exclusive jurisdiction over certain transactions on designated contract markets but 'does not contain express preemption language.'
insights.speaker: Jon Brodkin
insights.so_what: The absence of express preemption text is the load-bearing legal weakness in the entire prediction-market-versus-states defense.
insights.quote: does not contain express preemption language
insights.locator: The US law gives the CFTC exclusive jurisdiction

insights.claim: The judge relied on statutory language stating that nothing in the section shall supersede or limit the jurisdiction conferred on the SEC or other regulatory authorities under the laws of any State, nor the jurisdiction of courts of any State.
insights.speaker: Jon Brodkin
insights.so_what: This savings clause is the specific hook other state courts will cite; it makes a nationwide federal shield unlikely without new legislation.
insights.quote: The language referenced above indicates that Congress did not intend to supersede or limit States in regulating gambling
insights.locator: The judge pointed to a portion of the US law

insights.claim: To obtain the preliminary injunction Washington had to show likelihood of success on the merits, and the judge found the state likely to succeed in proving Kalshi violated both state gambling law and consumer protection law.
insights.speaker: Jon Brodkin
insights.so_what: A merits-likelihood finding, not a procedural technicality, means the final ruling probably lands the same way.
insights.locator: To get a preliminary injunction, a plaintiff must show

insights.claim: The court found that Kalshi advertisements claiming it offers 'legal betting' in Washington are likely to mislead a reasonable consumer, converting the marketing itself into an unfair or deceptive act in trade or commerce.
insights.speaker: Jon Brodkin
insights.so_what: Consumer-protection liability is a second, independent attack vector that survives even if preemption arguments eventually win.
insights.quote: that it offers 'legal betting' in Washington state are likely to mislead a reasonable consumer
insights.locator: McHale found that Kalshi ads claiming

insights.claim: Kalshi is neither licensed by the Washington state Gambling Commission nor registered to conduct business in Washington, per the court order.
insights.speaker: Jon Brodkin
insights.so_what: Operating unlicensed in a state is the simplest fact pattern for enforcement — replicable in every state where Kalshi lacks a license.
insights.locator: Kalshi is not licensed by the state Gambling Commission

themes.theme: Federal-state conflict and the Trump administration wildcard

insights.claim: Kalshi's core legal position is that it need not follow state laws because the CFTC has exclusive jurisdiction over prediction markets, an argument the Trump administration has repeatedly made and used to sue states that try to regulate the platforms.
insights.speaker: Jon Brodkin
insights.so_what: Federal executive backing is Kalshi's main asset in this fight and is political, not statutory — it can reverse with an administration.
insights.quote: Kalshi is regulated by the CFTC, which has exclusive jurisdiction over our exchange
insights.locator: Kalshi argues that it doesn't have to follow state laws

insights.claim: The CFTC declared a 'market emergency' in New York at Kalshi's request and ordered the company to continue operating in the state, an attempt to block New York from enforcing its gambling laws.
insights.speaker: Jon Brodkin
insights.so_what: A federal regulator using emergency powers to compel a firm to keep operating against state law is an escalation that invites a definitive appellate showdown.
insights.quote: The CFTC this week declared a "market emergency" in New York in an attempt to stop the state from enforcing its gambling laws against Kalshi.
insights.locator: One of Kalshi's legal options is asking the Trump administration for help

insights.claim: CFTC Chairman Michael Selig frames the dispute as Congress not intending derivatives exchanges to be regulated under a patchwork of state gaming laws, while courts across the country are actively splitting on what Congress intended.
insights.speaker: Jon Brodkin
insights.so_what: Regulatory-intent assertions from the CFTC chair carry no weight against a savings clause; a legislative fix, not rhetoric, is the only clean resolution.
insights.quote: Congress did not intend for derivatives exchanges to be regulated under a patchwork of state gaming laws

insights.claim: The dispute between states, the US government and Kalshi is being litigated simultaneously in state and federal courts throughout the country, meaning the outcome will be a patchwork until an appellate or Supreme Court resolution.
insights.speaker: Jon Brodkin
insights.so_what: Expect state-by-state geofencing costs and revenue attrition for prediction markets for multiple quarters before any unified answer.
insights.quote: The battle involving states, the US government, and Kalshi is being litigated in state and federal courts throughout the country.
insights.locator: The Trump administration has repeatedly made the same argument

insights.claim: Kalshi's platform lets consumers bet on thousands of topics including sports, political elections, entertainment, popular culture, and whether public figures will utter specific words or phrases, a breadth the court used to characterize it as an online betting platform advertised as a 'prediction market.'
insights.speaker: Jon Brodkin
insights.so_what: The wider the contract catalog drifts from economic hedging, the easier courts find it to classify the venue as gambling.
insights.quote: Kalshi operates an online betting platform that it advertises as a 'prediction market'

insights.claim: A Kalshi spokesperson counters that the company has never offered markets on wildfires because they create perverse incentives, and has never offered markets on war, death, or terrorism.
insights.speaker: Jon Brodkin
insights.so_what: Kalshi is defending on self-imposed ethical limits, an implicit acknowledgment that contract-catalog optics drive its regulatory risk.
insights.locator: The spokesperson added that Kalshi has never offered markets on wildfires

insights.claim: Washington AG Nick Brown asserts Kalshi got rich promoting wagers on sports, elections, natural disasters and events related to the Iran War — a characterization that conflicts with Kalshi's own statement that it never offered markets on war.
insights.speaker: Jon Brodkin
insights.so_what: A factual dispute over what Kalshi actually listed will shape both litigation credibility and headline risk.
insights.quote: Kalshi has gotten rich promoting wagers on sports, elections, natural disasters, events related to the Iran War, and more.
